what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Agents bring every skill and go in all directions, so they need containment, people, and pull requests between teams.
sections.para: Agents differ from people: uncontained they cause technical debt, yet each brings every skill, so the historian's brief also asks for data science, design, development and architecture. Role files and repository boundaries contain them, and people give focus, sometimes slowing things down. Teams should send each other pull requests, explorer code that villagers and town planners later refactor or replace.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Agents need direction, bring every skill, must be contained, and should send other teams pull requests.
sections.para: Uncontained agents cause damage, but every agent brings every skill. That power needs scope, guidelines and agents guiding agents. People give focus and ownership, and slowing down pays: the refactoring is cheaper because automation did not go too far. Teams should hand each other explorer code as pull requests.

sections.label: Different from people, in good ways and bad
sections.line: Agents can go in all directions, so they need direction; the villager exists because of that.
sections.para: Agents' breadth lets them do a lot and cause damage. The PHP story needed a villager because many task-focused agents created technical debt: every release rewrites about two thousand files, and 28 release messages since 23 October name a conflict, collision or renumbering.

sections.label: One role, every skill
sections.line: A focused agent also brings every other skill: the historian is asked to be five roles at once.
sections.para: Each agent runs on a model that can reason, learn and fetch data, so it can do work beyond its focus. The historian's new brief asks for history plus data science, design, development and architecture, work that would need five people in a human team, while the agent also understands Git and the team's primitives.

sections.label: Contained
sections.line: Role files contain each agent today; six repositories will make GitHub enforce the boundary.
sections.para: The historian's role file lists its exclusive paths, append-only shared files, pages and what needs the editor's approval. Splitting the site into six repositories turns that expectation into a GitHub boundary. Containment also means agents passing guidance to each other, which quickly gets complex.

sections.label: Where the people come in
sections.line: People give focus and ownership, and the editor as bottleneck makes room to think: go slow to go fast.
sections.para: Being a bottleneck gives time to think and refactor. The one-into-six refactoring is cheaper because the team did not automate too far first. Iteration, features and experiments are now very fast, and some tools are still underused because effort goes to the points of highest leverage, which is human work.

sections.label: Teams that send each other pull requests
sections.line: Agents should build what they need as explorers and send it to the owning team as a pull request.
sections.para: An old principle, contributing to other teams rather than only asking, rarely worked in companies and partly in open source, but agents can scale it. An agent builds what it needs in its own space and sends it as a pull request; villagers refactor it, and town planners later replace it. Today agents only append and message: 26 messages so far.

sections.label: What exists, and what is proposed
sections.line: Scoped role files, messages and the six-repository plan exist; the historian's brief and pull requests between teams are proposed.
sections.para: Existing: focused agents with scope in their role files, messages between agents, the proposed villager and the agreed plan to split into six repositories. Proposed: the historian's expanded brief, pull requests between agent teams, and GitHub enforcing repository owners.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Skills are the model's; numbers come from the villager article; no agent pull request exists yet.
sections.para: Output quality still depends on the brief and review. Release and conflict figures come from the PHP site's history as counted earlier. No agent has yet sent another team a pull request.

sections.line: A voice memo and the PHP site's historian role file, agent messages and six-repository plan.
sections.para: The editor's memo of 25 October 2026 and the PHP story site at v0.22.0: the historian's role file, agent messages, and the dev agent's proposal and plan, with related newsroom articles.
